steps.decide: Which fields the job actually requires, and which are merely nice
Label and help placement, and whether the label is visible at all times
When validation runs and what each message says
Error announcement and focus movement for assistive technology

rules.statement: A field that does not change a decision is removed; the form asks only what the task needs.
Labels stay visible at all times; placeholder text never substitutes for a label because it disappears exactly when it is needed.
Validation runs on blur and on submit; as-you-type errors are limited to formats the user cannot get right by finishing.
An error says what is wrong and how to fix it in the user's terms (Use 8 characters or more), never Invalid input.
Errors are announced through a live region and the first invalid field receives focus on submit; colour is never the only error signal.

motion.noneReason: a spinner beside a field competes with the caret
motion.reducedMotion: the field keeps its text; the pending state is textual

motion.noneReason: error text must be readable the moment it is true
a cleared error needs no animation to be understood
moving an error under a caret distracts from the fix

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: validation results for an older value are ignored; the field shows the verdict for what it currently contains

sections.intent: Collect exactly what the task needs and tell the user how to fix a problem without losing their work.

alternatives: Inline validation on blur is preferable to a summary-only error list
